positiveFlows.title: HURRICANE HELENE LEFT A SWATH OF DESTRUCTION ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST, IMPACTING AN AREA STRETCHING FROM THE GULF COAST TO THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS. TIMBER DAMAGE ESTIMATES RANGE FROM HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS OF DOLLARS TO OVER $1 BILLION IN THE AFFECTED STATES. IN THE WAKE OF HELENE FEDERAL, STATE, INDUSTRY AND PRIVATE LAND MANAGERS ARE FACED WITH MANY CHALLENGES. THESE INCLUDE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH INSECT PESTS AND FOREST PATHOGENS FOLLOWING DISTURBANCE, THE NATURE AND SEVERITY OF DAMAGE AS IT RELATES TO FOREST STRUCTURE AND COMPOSITION, TREE-LEVEL DECLINE AND MORTALITY OVER TIME DUE TO SUBLETHAL DAMAGE, AND RISK OF INVASIVE PLANT SPREAD DUE TO HABITAT CHANGES AND MANAGEMENT INTERVENTIONS. INVASION BY NON-NATIVE PLANTS CAUSES A WIDE ARRAY OF DETRIMENTAL IMPACTS TO U.S. FOREST ECOSYSTEMS, INCLUDING THE DEGRADATION OF WILDLIFE HABITAT, CHANGES TO ECOSYSTEM FUNCTIONS, AND ALTERATIONS TO NUTRIENT, CARBON AND WATER CYCLES. THIS AGREEMENT WILL ALLOW FOR CONDUCTING ASSESSMENTS OF THE RISK OF INVASIVE PLANT ESTABLISHMENT AND SPREAD WITHIN HELENE-AFFECTED FORESTS USING A VARIETY OF FIELD-COLLECTED AND REMOTELY SENSED DATA; PROVIDING DECISION SUPPORT FOR THE MANAGEMENT AND RESTORATION OF THESE FORESTS RELATING TO THE CONTROL OF INVASIVE PLANT ESTABLISHMENT AND SPREAD; AND COMMUNICATING WITH PARTNERS WITHIN THE FOREST SERVICE AND IN OTHER AGENCIES TO SHARE RESULTS.

TO ANALYZE DATA ON WILDLAND FUELS IN AREAS AFFECTED BY HURRICANE HELENE (SOUTHERN APPALACHIAN FORESTED REGION), RUN COMPUTER MODELS OF FIRE BEHAVIOR, AND WORK WITH MANAGERS TO UNDERSTAND HURRICANE DAMAGE AND EFFECTS ON FUTURE FIRE MANAGEMENT AND IMPROVE FUELS MONITORING EFFORTS. DAMAGE CAUSED BY HURRICANE HELENE IS PROFOUND AND WE NOW CAN DO AN ACCURATE ASSESSMENT OF THE HURRICANE DAMAGE, INCLUDING CHANGE IN HAZARDOUS FUELS CONDITIONS USING NEW TECHNOLOGIES (TERRESTRIAL LASER SCANNING), FIELD SAMPLING, AND EMERGING FIRE BEHAVIOR MODELS AND ANALYZE THEM USING SOPHISTICATED COMPUTER PROGRAMS. DATA WILL BE TRANSLATED AND NEW 3D FUELS METRICS FOR USE IN NEXT-GENERATION PHYSICS-BASED FIRE BEHAVIOR MODELS AND WORK WITH MANAGEMENT (CO-PRODUCTION) TO EXAMINE FIRE BEHAVIOR IN DAMAGED AREAS. THIS WILL BUILD PATHWAYS TO LINK THESE UNIQUE (DAMAGED FOREST) FUELS DATA TO FIRE BEHAVIOR MODELS AND PROVIDE ESTIMATES OF FIRE BEHAVIOR IN THESE DAMAGED AREAS. COSTS COVER SALARY, EQUIPMENT AND SUPPLIES FOR RESEARCH. THE COOPERATOR COMPRISES A PARTNERSHIP OF THREE RESEARCH UNIVERSITIES IN NEW MEXICO.

THE SRS AND NCS WILL COLLABORATE TO RE-INVENTORY THE PERMANENT PLOTS ON BCEF AND USE THE PRE- AND POST-HELENE DATA TO ASSESS HOW FOREST STRUCTURE, COMPOSITION, AND FUNCTION ARE AFFECTED BY EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS ACROSS A COMPLEX LANDSCAPE CHARACTERIZED BY STRONG ENVIRONMENTAL GRADIENTS, WITH IMPLICATIONS EXTENDING TO THE BROADER APPALACHIAN REGION. THE POST-HELENE INVENTORY WILL PROVIDE DATA AND CONTEXT THAT WILL AID IN FOREST RECOVERY AND REHABILITATION EFFORTS. ADDITIONALLY, THE INFORMATION PRODUCED WILL INFORM NEW MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES AND/OR PROVIDE SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION THAT SUPPORTS EXISTING PRACTICES USED TO MITIGATE OR INCREASE RESILIENCE OF SOUTHEASTERN OAK/HICKORY FORESTS TO CHANGING CLIMATE, INCLUDING EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS. THE RESULTS WILL BE PARTICULARLY MEANINGFUL IN THE CONTEXT OF OAK RESTORATION AND MANAGEMENT. MODIFICATIONS TO FOREST STRUCTURE CAN ALTER SUCCESSIONAL TRAJECTORIES AND MODIFY OAK REGENERATION POTENTIAL. WHETHER OAK REGENERATION POTENTIAL IS REDUCED OR IMPROVED WILL IMPACT THE TYPE, FREQUENCY, AND INTENSITY OF MANAGEMENT ACTIONS NEEDED TO SUSTAIN OAK ON STORM-AFFECTED PORTIONS OF THE LANDSCAPE.

THIS WORK IS IN SUPPORT OF HURRICANE HELENE RECOVERY. THE COLLABORATION WILL GREATLY FACILITATE DEVELOPMENT OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TAKING ADVANTAGE OF SPECIALIZED SKILLS, RESOURCES, AND LABOR AS WELL AS EXPERTISE IN FOREST HEALTH RELATED TO CATASTROPHIC WIND DAMAGE. OUR APPROACH REDUCES RELIANCE ON DIRECT HIRING OR CONTRACT LABOR, WHICH IS FINANCIALLY AND ADMINISTRATIVELY BURDENSOME. THIS WORK BUILDS ON PRIOR COLLABORATIVE WORK IN THE WAKE OF HURRICANE MICHAEL, AND OTHER WORK USING TORNADOES AS A SURROGATE SYSTEM FOR EXAMINING WINDEFFECTS ON FOREST HEALTH. THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE A RAPID ASSESSMENT OF SHORT-TERM TREE MORTALITY AND DIEBACK, IMPACTS OF DAMAGING INSECTS AND PATHOGENS, LONGER-TERM RESIDUAL TREE LEVEL EFFECTS,DELAYED MORTALITY, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR DAMAGING INSECTS AND DISEASE, AND PROVIDE TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER FOR BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR TIMBER PRODUCTION AND SALVAGE IN RESPONSE TOFUTURE EVENTS. THE FUNDS WILL SUPPORT PERSONNEL FACULTY AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, MATERIALS AND SUPPLIES, AND TRAVEL NECESSARY TO CONDUCT THE WORK.

THE PRIMARY GOAL ASSOCIATED WITH THE AGREEMENT IS TO USE EXISTING GAP-BASED SILVICULTURAL TREATMENTS (BOTH EXPERIMENTAL GAPS AND OPERATIONALLY-CREATED GAPS) TO IDENTIFY CONDITIONS WHERE OAK SEEDLINGS ARE MOST LIKELY TO DEVELOP INTO LARGE, COMPETITIVE SEEDLINGS AT LANDSCAPE LEVELS POST-HELENE. EMPIRICAL DATA AND RESULTANT MODELS FROM EXPERIMENTAL AND OPERATIONAL GAPS WILL BE APPLIED AT LANDSCAPE-LEVELS TO POST-HELENE FOREST DAMAGE ASSESSMENTS. COUPLING EMPIRICAL DATA/MODELS WITH LANDSCAPE-LEVEL MODELS OF FOREST DAMAGE WILL IDENTIFY AT LARGE SPATIAL SCALES WHERE OAK FOCUSED SILVICULTURE PRACTICES COULD BE IMPLEMENTED IN EFFORTS TO REGENERATE AND RECRUIT ECONOMICALLY-VALUABLE OAK SPECIES AFTER A SEVERE DISTURBANCE, THEREBY ENSURING A SUSTAINABLE SUPPLY OF HIGH-VALUE HARDWOOD SAWTIMBER AND SUPPORT FOR RURAL ECONOMIES THROUGH THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT AND RESTORATION OF DISTURBANCE-IMPACTED FOREST RESOURCES.

SPECIFICALLY, WE AIM TO SUPPORT PACIFIC NORTHWEST FIA PLOT MEASUREMENTS, INCLUDING DATA COLLECTION, QUALITY ASSURANCE AND QUALITY CONTROL, AND DATA ARCHIVING, AS WELL ASREGIONAL AND NATIONAL FIA REPORTING AND RESEARCH OBJECTIVES.

THIS PROJECT WILL BE COLLECTING FIELD DATA ON HAZARDOUS WILDLAND FUELS IN AREAS AFFECTED BY HURRICANE HELENE (SOUTHERN APPALACHIAN FORESTED REGION), WHILE WORKING WITH FOREST AND FUELS MANAGERS TO IMPROVE FUELS MONITORING PROGRAMS. THIS NEW AGREEMENT IS NEEDED BECAUSE THE DAMAGE CAUSED BY HURRICANE HELENE HAS CHANGED HAZARDOUS FUELS CONDITIONS DRASTICALLY, AND HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED USING FIELD METHODS AND NEW TECHNOLOGIES (TERRESTRIAL LASER SCANNING). THE PROJECT WILL ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF HURRICANE HELENE ON CHANGE IN FOREST STRUCTURE AND HAZARDOUS WILDLAND FUELS CONDITIONS THAT ARE CONDUCIVE TO WILDFIRE.

THIS RESEARCH PROJECT WILL STUDY THE NEEDS OF FAMILY FARMERS AND FOREST OWNERS IN RECOVERING FROM HURRICANE DAMAGE TO THEIR WOODLANDS, UNDERSTANDING OF HOW FAMILY FARMERS AND FOREST OWNERS RESPOND TO HURRICANE DAMAGE ON THEIR WOODLANDS, INCLUDING WHAT OPPORTUNITIES THEY HAVE FOR MEANINGFUL ECONOMIC RECOVERY. UNDERSTANDING WHERE THOSE OPPORTUNITIES MAY BE LACKING ALONG WITH WAYS IN WHICH THE LOCAL, STATE, AND FEDERAL GOVERNMENT, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE NON-PROFIT AND PRIVATE SECTORS, CAN WORK TOGETHER TO AID FAMILY FOREST OWNERS RECOVERY FROM HURRICANE DAMAGE AND PREPARE FOR FUTURE HURRICANES.

THE PROJECT EVALUATES THE IMPACTS OF SALVAGE ON TIMBER MARKETS, PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNER AND NATIONAL FOREST RESPONSES, AND POTENTIAL FOR INNOVATIONS TO USE SALVAGED WOOD. THE PROJECT GOALS WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH COOPERATION BETWEEN USFS, UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA, AND UNIVERSITY OF MASSACHUSETTS. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES ASSESSMENT NEEDS PERTAINING TO HURRICANES, CONSISTENT WITH PUBLIC LAW NO: 118-158. THE RESEARCH ADDRESSES THE AGENCY PRIORITY AREA OF TIMBER BY ASSESSING MARKET IMPACTS RELATED TO THE STORM AND FALLS UNDER HUMAN AND NATURAL DISTURBANCES AND MARKETS AND TRADE RESEARCH PERFORMED BY THE RESEARCH WORK UNIT SCIENTISTS.

THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE (USDA) FOREST SERVICE FIA (FOREST INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS) PROGRAM IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF FIELD-COLLECTED TIMBER INFORMATION FOR THE WHOLE UNITED STATES. DATA PROVIDED BY FIA ARE BROADLY USED TO SUPPORT NATIONAL GOALS ARTICULATED IN EXECUTIVE ORDER (EO) 14225, IMMEDIATE EXPANSION OF AMERICAN TIMBER PRODUCTION AND IN THE SUBSEQUENT USDA SECRETARY'S MEMO (SM) 1078-006 INCREASING TIMBER PRODUCTION AND DESIGNATING AN EMERGENCY SITUATION ON NATIONAL FOREST SYSTEM LANDS.HOWEVER, ANALYSIS OF FIA DATA REQUIRES ADVANCED UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROGRAMS DATABASE AND CAN BE SLOW FOLLOWING NATURAL EVENTS SUCH AS WILDFIRES AND HURRICANES THAT DEMAND RAPID SALVAGE AND RECOVERY EFFORTS. OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET (OMB) MEMORANDUM M-25-22 DRIVING EFFICIENT ACQUISITION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN GOVERNMENT REQUIRES THAT FEDERAL AGENCIES MUST BOTH: 1) REMOVE BARRIERS TO INNOVATION AND PROVIDE THE BEST VALUE FOR THE TAXPAYER;, AND 2) EMPOWER AI (ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE) LEADERS TO ACCELERATE RESPONSIBLE AI ADOPTION.THIS AGREEMENT WITH THE COOPERATOR WOULD BOTH PILOT A NATURAL LANGUAGE AI THAT WILL ALLOW PUBLIC USERS TO QUERY FIAS DATABASE DIRECTLY WITHOUT HAVING TO LEARN QUERY SYNTAX, AND, CREATE A RAPID-RESPONSE ANALYTICAL PIPELINE THAT WILL USE INITIAL MAPS OF HURRICANE/WILDFIRE EXTENT TO MAKE CREDIBLE ESTIMATES OF THE FOREST RESOURCES AT RISK. THESE GOALS WILL INCREASE THE VALUE OF THE COUNTRYS INVESTMENT IN FOREST INVENTORY BY MAKING ASSESSMENTS MORE ACCESSIBLE AND MORE TIMELY.THIS APPLIED RESEARCH WILL TAKE PLACE BOTH ON THE CAMPUS OF THE COOPERATOR AND AT THE FACILITIES OF FIAS REGIONAL HEADQUARTERS IN RIVERDALE, UTAH. FIA EXPECTS TO TAKE DELIVERY OF PILOT INSTANCES OF BOTH A NATURAL LANGUAGE QUERY TOOL AND A RAPID-RESPONSE RESOURCE ANALYSIS TOOL BY THE END OF CALENDAR YEAR 2026. FIA ANALYSIS AND RESEARCH STAFF WILL PERFORM A TECHNICAL EVALUATION WITHIN 3 MONTHS FOLLOWING DELIVERY, AND WILL FORWARD RECOMMENDATIONS RELATED TO THE USE OF AI-POWERED QUERY TOOLS TO NATIONAL LEADERSHIP.

RESEARCH INTEGRATING A MIXED-METHODS APPROACH TO COMPREHENSIVELY EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF HURRICANES ON THE SOUTHERN FOREST SECTOR AND REGIONAL ECONOMY. TO ANALYZE DATA COLLECTED FROM RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WITH LOGGERS AND TIMBER BUYERS TO SOLICIT INFORMATION ON USAGE OF SALVAGE TIMBER AND PERCEPTIONS FOLLOWING HURRICANE EVENTS; EXPLORE THE AVAILABILITY OF TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES USED TO ASSESS DAMAGE FROM HURRICANES; AND CONDUCT COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC ANALYSES TO ASSESS POTENTIAL ECONOMY-WIDE IMPACTS OF HURRICANE HELENE ON THE US SOUTH. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE AT LEAST ONE JOURNAL ARTICLE, TWO OR MORE PRESENTATIONS AT A PROFESSIONAL MEETING OR CONFERENCE, AND AN EXTENSION PUBLICATION.

THIS PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE AND QUANTIFY THE ECONOMIC LOSSES ASSOCIATED WITH HURRICANE HELENE TO WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA'S RECREATION ECONOMY. THE PROPOSED EFFORT LEVERAGES THE 2023 WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA OUTDOOR RECREATION PARTICIPATION SURVEY CONDUCTED BY APPALACHIAN STATE UNIVERSITY IN 2023 PRE-HELENE. FUNDING WILL ENABLE COOPERATORS TO DISSEMINATE AND ANALYZE A REPEAT SURVEY PANEL CONDUCTED IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE PAPERWORK REDUCTION ACT TO ASSESS CHANGES IN VISITATION PATTERNS, TRIP FREQUENCY, AND SPENDING BEHAVIOR PRE-AND-POST HELENE. BY LEVERAGING THIS UNIQUE BASELINE DATASET, THE PROJECT WILL QUANTIFY ECONOMIC LOSSES TO THE REGION'S OUTDOOR RECREATION ECONOMY RESULTING FROM STORM-RELATED INFRASTRUCTURE DAMAGE ACROSS 25 COUNTIES AND THE QUALLA BOUNDARY IN WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA. THESE INSIGHTS WILL INFORM RECOVERY STRATEGIES, GUIDE INFRASTRUCTURE INVESTMENTS, AND SUPPORT FOREST SERVICE MISSION GOALS AROUND RURAL PROSPERITY, RECREATION ACCESS, AND DISASTER RESILIENCE.

RECENT MAJOR HURRICANES LIKE HELENE AND MILTON HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACTED SOUTHERN FORESTS AND ASSOCIATED MARKETS. THIS RESEARCH STANDS TO USE GLOBAL MODEL FRAMEWORK, ACCOUNTING FOR INTERNATIONAL TRADE AND MARKET LINKAGES TO FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW FOREST PRODUCT MARKETS RESPOND TO THESE DISTURBANCES, PARTICULARLY REGARDING DEMAND-SIDE IMPACTS FROM POST-HURRICANE REBUILDING ACTIVITIES AND THEIR BROADER EMPLOYMENT EFFECTS. THE PROJECT WILL COVER SALARY, TRAVEL, AND SUPPLIES TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT AND PRESENT METHODOLOGIES.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO GENERATE ESTIMATES OF THE PROPORTION OF TOTAL TIMBER LOSS FROM HURRICANES HELENE AND MILTON, AND POSSIBLY OTHER RECENT HURRICANES, THAT PRIVATE FOREST LANDOWNERS MAY BE ABLE TO RECOVER THROUGH CASUALTY LOSS DEDUCTIONS IN THE FEDERAL INCOME TAX CODE. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE LANDOWNERS AND LANDOWNER ASSOCIATIONS INFORMATION TO PREPARE FOR FUTURE DISASTERS BY HAVING A BETTER SENSE OF WHAT THEY CAN EXPECT TO RECOVER AND ALLOW DECISION-MAKERS A BETTER SENSE OF HOW TO RESPOND.

THE STUDY WILL EVALUATE IMPACTS TO TIMBER PRICES RELATED TO HURRICANES HELENE AND MILTON. THE PURPOSE OF THIS AGREEMENT IS TO COLLECT AND DISSEMINATE DATA PERTAINING TO STUMPAGE PRICES FOR A SPATIAL DISPERSION OF LOCAL STUMPAGE MARKETS. TIME SERIES ECONOMETRIC MODELS WILL THEN BE DEVELOPED TO EVALUATE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL LINKAGES, AND PRODUCT FORM MARKET SEGMENTS.

THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE FOREST SERVICE FOREST INVENTORY AND ANALYSIS (FIA) PROGRAM IS MANDATED BY STATUTE (16 U.S.C. 1642E) TO PROVIDE ACCURATE AND TIMELY INFORMATION ON THE STATUS AND TRENDS OF OUR NATION'S PRIVATE AND PUBLIC FORESTS THROUGH INVENTORIES OF TREES ACROSS ALL LANDS, LANDOWNERS, AND WOOD PROCESSING MILLS. THIS AGREEMENT FUNDS A PARTNERSHIP WITH ALASKA DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES, DIVISION OF FORESTRY AND FIRE PROTECTION TO SAMPLE THE FORESTS IN ALASKA WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE INTERIOR ALASKA FIA UNIT. THIS INCLUDES HIRING THE MAJORITY OF FIELD SAMPLING CREW MEMBERS AND CREW LEADERS, MANAGING THE HELICOPTER CONTRACT TO GET TO PLOT, COORDINATING TRAVEL FOR EMPLOYEES AND ALL THE EQUIPMENT IN AND OUT OF EACH HUB, FINDING AND PROVIDING WORK/LAB SPACE IN EACH OF THE HUBS FOR ADEQUATE WORK SPACE, SUPPLY THE MAJORITY OF THE EQUIPMENT AS PART OF THE FIA PROGRAMS NATIONWIDE FOREST INVENTORY (NFI). THESE EFFORTS PROVIDE INFORMATION TO LAND MANAGERS THAT CAN BE USED FOR INFORMED DECISION MAKING, INCLUDING DATA FOR DETERMINING THE VOLUME, SPECIES AND SIZE DISTRIBUTION OF AVAILABLE TIMBER. FIA PROVIDES THE FOUNDATIONAL FOREST DATA FOR LANDFIRE, THE KEY VEGETATION AND FUELS SOURCE FOR THE 2023 WILDFIRE HAZARD POTENTIAL FOR THE UNITED STATES, AND SUPPORTS THE HEALTHY FOREST RESTORATION ACT OF 2003 (P.L. 108-148, 601) BY COLLECTING INFORMATION ON MONUMENTED PLOTS ACROSS ALL FEDERAL, STATE, AND PRIVATE LANDS ACROSS THE U.S.
